items.seoTitle: FBR POS Integration in Pakistan: 2026 Guide for Shops
items.seoDescription: Who must integrate their POS with FBR, what the invoice must carry, why a licensed integrator matters, and the penalties for not integrating.
items.title: FBR POS integration,
items.description: Not every shop has to connect its POS to FBR, but the ones that do face real penalties if they do not. Here is who is affected, what the law asks for on the invoice, and what to check before you choose software.

faq.q: Does every shop have to integrate its POS with FBR?
faq.a: No. The law requires it of Tier-1 retailers and of other registered persons the FBR notifies. The Tier-1 definition lists several categories, such as units of national or international chains. Ask your tax consultant or check the Sales Tax Act definition to see whether you are covered.

faq.q: Can any POS software connect to FBR?
faq.a: FBR's rules say integration must be carried out through a licensed integrator. FBR's own PRAL can act as one and may provide the integration free of cost. Ask any POS vendor exactly how its integration works and which licensed integrator is involved. ZAP POS holds an FBR integrator licence.

faq.q: What must the receipt show?
faq.a: A unique FBR invoice number and a QR code that customers can scan to verify the bill, along with the sales tax details the rules list.

faq.q: Is Punjab's PRA system the same as FBR's?
faq.a: No. Punjab Revenue Authority runs its own electronic invoice monitoring system for businesses such as restaurants and hotels in Punjab. FBR and provincial authorities have separate rules, so check which authority your business falls under.

items.ctaTitle: Want to see FBR-ready billing?
items.ctaText: Book a free demo and we'll show you how ZAP POS prints FBR invoice numbers and QR codes.
items.shortAnswer: Tier-1 retailers and other persons notified by FBR must connect their POS to FBR through a licensed integrator, issue invoices with an FBR invoice number and QR code, and risk penalties and sealing of premises if they do not. Punjab has a separate system, PRA's e-IMS, for restaurants and similar businesses.

p: FBR requires Tier-1 retailers to connect their outlets to its computerised system so sales are reported in real time. The Sales Tax Act defines Tier-1 retailers by category; the first listed is a retailer that is a unit of a national or international chain of stores, and the definition names other categories as well. FBR also integrates other registered persons it notifies, and its published figures show restaurants and textile and leather retailers being connected as separate groups.

A single small shop is often not covered, but do not assume. Read the definition of Tier-1 retailer in the Sales Tax Act or ask your tax consultant, because the answer depends on your category and on notifications that change.

article.h: What the electronic invoice must carry
p: The rules require a real-time, verifiable electronic sales tax invoice for every sale. The system sends the invoice data to FBR, receives a unique FBR invoice number, and the receipt prints a QR code built from that number so a customer can check the bill. The invoice also carries the sales tax details the rules list, such as the amount of tax, any discount, a reference number and units of measurement.
Sales through card, QR or other digital payment must also be accepted at the counter, and a bill without the invoice number or QR code is exactly what inspectors look for.

Since the rules were changed in December 2023, nobody may carry out integration of registered persons through software unless FBR has licensed them as an integrator. FBR's FAQs repeat that notified persons must integrate through a licensed integrator. PRAL, FBR's technology arm, can act as a licensed integrator and may provide integration and downloadable software free of cost when asked.
In practice this means you should ask your POS vendor three things: which licensed integrator carries your invoices, what it costs you, and who is responsible if the connection fails.

article.h: What happens if you do not integrate
p: For a Tier-1 retailer that is not integrated, the rules allow the Commissioner to take action that includes a penalty under the Sales Tax Act and sealing the business premises until the penalty is paid and every POS in every branch is integrated. Issuing invoices without the prescribed number or QR code, or with a duplicate number, can also lead to proceedings. Read the rules or ask a consultant for the current penalty amounts, because they are set in the law and can change.

Provincial taxes on services are collected by provincial authorities, and each has its own system. In Punjab, the Punjab Revenue Authority requires hotels, restaurants, coffee shops and marriage halls to issue computerised receipts through its Electronic Invoice Monitoring System, e-IMS, with a unique invoice number and a PRA QR code. Reports in 2026 put fines for non-compliance between Rs 400,000 and Rs 1 million. An earlier amendment set the threshold for restaurants at Rs 6 million of annual revenue. PRA has also been working to link e-IMS with FBR's POS system so businesses need one integration instead of two.
Sindh and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have their own revenue authorities too. Check which authority your business falls under before you decide.

article.h: A checklist before you choose software
p: 1. Confirm which authority you report to, FBR or a provincial authority, and whether you are required to integrate.
2. Register your outlets and each POS with that authority.
3. Ask the vendor which licensed integrator is used, and what happens if you change vendor.
4. Check that every receipt shows the invoice number and QR code, and scan one with the official verification app.
5. Check that returns are reported as credit notes against the original bill.
6. Ask what happens when the internet is down: how bills are saved and when they are sent.
7. Keep your records. The rules expect invoice data to be preserved.

ZAP POS is an FBR-licensed integrator, so the integration is built into the software and handled by us. You enter your own POS ID and token, and every receipt prints FBR's invoice number with a QR code. Returns are sent as credit notes against the original bill, each way of paying gets its own tax rate, and when the internet drops billing carries on and the bills are sent once the connection is back.
We set it up with you, so you do not need a separate integration tool. Ask us for a demo and we will show it on your own shop's settings.

This guide is a summary, not legal or tax advice, and the rules change. Check them at the source: the FBR POS Integration pages and POS Booklet at fbr.gov.pk, FBR's frequently asked questions on electronic invoicing, SRO 69(I)/2025 on electronic invoicing, and Punjab Revenue Authority notices on e-IMS. Business Recorder, Dawn and Express Tribune have reported the integration numbers and enforcement actions mentioned here.

article.h: Start with how your shop really runs
p: Before comparing features, write down three things: how many counters you bill from, how many branches you have or plan to open, and what you sell (packed goods with [barcode](/barcode-system-for-your-shop)s, loose items by weight, medicines with expiry dates, food that goes to a kitchen). Every question below is easier once you know this.

article.h: 1. Does billing stop when the internet drops?
p: In Pakistan the router often goes off during [load shedding](/billing-during-load-shedding), even when the PC is on a UPS. Some POS systems keep everything online and stop billing without internet. Ask where the shop's data is kept. If it is on your own PC, billing can continue offline and sync later.
In the demo, unplug the internet and make a bill. If the queue would stop in your shop, it will stop in the demo too.

article.h: 2. Is it ready for FBR or PRA?
p: If you are required to report sales, the POS should send each bill to FBR (or your provincial authority) and print the invoice number and QR code on the receipt. Ask three follow-ups: what happens to reporting when the internet is down, how refunds are reported, and how it avoids sending the same bill twice.

article.h: 3. Can several counters share one stock?
p: With more than one counter, every counter should see the same stock within seconds, and an item that has run out should not be billed twice. Ask what happens when the main PC is switched off: do the other counters stop, or keep billing?

article.h: 4. Will your printers and scanners work?
p: Most shops use standard thermal receipt printers, USB barcode scanners and cash drawers. Some also need label printers or kitchen printers. Bring your own hardware details to the demo and ask to see a receipt and a label print.

article.h: 5. Does it fit the way you sell?
p: Check the details that matter to your trade: packs like dozens and cartons, items sold by weight, expiry dates for medicines and food, kitchen stations for restaurants, and sizes and colours for clothing and shoes. A POS that can't model your products forces staff to work around it.

Most cash leaks at the counter: discounts below cost, cancelled bills and quiet refunds. Look for staff logins, manager approval for big discounts, and a record of every cancelled order with who did it.
Ask where backups are kept, how often they are taken, and how a restore works if a PC's disk fails. Your sales history is your business record, so make sure you can export it.

article.h: 8. Are the prices clear, in rupees?
p: Ask for the monthly and yearly price in PKR, what changes when you add counters or branches, and whether there are setup or hardware fees. Write it down so you can compare like with like.

article.h: 9. Who helps you, and how fast?
p: Setup, training and the odd problem on a busy evening all need a person who answers. Ask how support works (WhatsApp, phone, visits), in which language, and how updates are delivered.

article.h: 10. Test it like a real rush
p: Ask the seller to let you bill 20 items quickly, make a refund, apply a discount, close a shift and print a receipt, with the internet unplugged for part of it. Ten minutes of this tells you more than any brochure.

items.title: Register, Excel or POS?
items.description: Most shops start with a register or a spreadsheet, and many run well that way for years. Here is what each one does well, where it costs you money, and the signs that it is time to move to a POS.

p: A register is cheap, needs no electricity and everyone understands it. The trouble starts as the shop grows: long bills are added by hand, stock is counted only when something runs out, and the day's sale rarely matches the cash in the drawer exactly. Nobody can see the numbers unless they are standing at the counter.

A spreadsheet is a big step up for stock lists and monthly totals. But it is not built for the counter: two people can't safely edit the same file, a wrong formula can quietly change totals, and billing a customer in Excel is slow. Most shops end up with Excel for records and a register for billing, which means typing everything twice.

A POS does the billing and the records in one step. Each bill is added up for you and takes the items off stock, the cash drawer is counted per shift, and reports for the day are ready when you close. With more than one counter, every counter sees the same stock.

article.h: Signs it is time to switch
p: You run out of popular items before you notice. The cash in the drawer and the day's sale don't match and you can't tell why. You have a second counter or a second branch. You need to report sales to FBR or PRA. Staff discounts and cancelled bills worry you. If two of these sound familiar, a POS will pay for itself.

article.h: Moving over without stopping the shop
p: Start with your product list: most shops already have one in Excel, and it can be imported instead of typed in again. Print [barcode](/barcode-system-for-your-shop) labels for items without them, set up your printer and scanner, and run the POS alongside the register for a day or two. Then put the register away.

faq.a: Yes. Import your product list from Excel instead of typing it again, then add barcodes where needed.

faq.q: Is a POS worth it for a small shop?
faq.a: If you have more than a few hundred products, a second counter, or cash that rarely matches the day's sales, a POS usually pays for itself through fewer mistakes and better stock control.

faq.q: What if the power or internet goes?
faq.a: A POS needs power like any PC, so keep it on a UPS. ZAP POS doesn't need the internet to bill.

items.title: Cloud POS or offline-first POS,
items.description: Cloud-only and offline-first POS software both work, but they fail in different ways. Here is how they compare on internet drops, speed, branches, FBR and your data, so you can choose for your own shop.

faq.q: Does a cloud-only POS stop when the internet drops?
faq.a: It depends on the product. Some cloud POS apps keep a limited offline mode and some stop. Ask the vendor to show you a bill being made with the router switched off.

faq.q: Is an offline-first POS cut off from the cloud?
faq.a: No. An offline-first POS bills on your own computer and syncs to the cloud when the internet is available, so you can still see branches and reports.

faq.q: Which is better for several branches?
faq.a: Either can work. What matters is whether each branch keeps billing when its own internet drops, and whether stock and sales from every branch reach the owner afterwards.

faq.q: Can I switch later?
faq.a: Ask any vendor how you export your items, customers and sales history before you buy. You should be able to leave with your own data.

An offline-first POS bills on your own computer and syncs when the connection returns. For shops with unreliable internet, test what each one does with the router off.

article.h: Two ways to build a POS
p: A cloud-only POS runs mostly on the vendor's servers. Your counter opens it in a browser or an app and each sale goes online. An offline-first POS runs its billing on a computer in your shop and keeps a full local copy of the data. It syncs to the cloud when the internet allows, so owners can still see reports away from the shop.
Neither is always better. The right choice depends on how reliable your internet is, how many branches you have and how you want to hold your data.

This is the biggest difference in a Pakistani shop. Load shedding, a router left off or a weak connection will interrupt the internet at some point. With an offline-first design, billing carries on from the shop computer and the bills are sent later. With a cloud-only design, what happens depends on the product: some have a short offline mode, others wait for the connection.
Note that a power cut also switches off the computer unless it is on a UPS, so no software can promise billing in a blackout. The real question is what happens when only the internet goes down.

A local system answers from the shop computer, so scanning and billing do not wait on a network round trip. A cloud system can feel just as quick on a good connection and slow on a poor one. Test it at your busiest hour rather than trusting a demo.

Cloud-only products make it easy to see all branches in one place. Offline-first products can do the same once each branch syncs, with the benefit that a branch with a dead connection still sells. Ask both kinds: if one branch is offline for a day, what does the owner see, and what happens to stock when it reconnects?

Whatever you choose, check how the product reports to FBR or PRA, whether it prints the invoice number and QR code, and what it does when the authority's system or your internet is unreachable. Our FBR guide explains what the rules ask for.

With a cloud-only product your records sit on the vendor's servers. With offline-first you hold a copy in your own shop as well. In both cases ask how to export your items, customers and sales, and what happens to your data if you stop paying.
Compare the full price in rupees: monthly or yearly fees, setup, counters, branches, hardware and support. A cheap monthly price that excludes extra counters or support can cost more over a year.

If your internet is steady and you have one counter, either type will do. If your internet is unreliable or you have [several counters](/multi-counter-pos) or branches, offline-first deserves a serious test.

items.seoTitle: Billing During Load Shedding: Keep Your POS Running
items.seoDescription: What keeps billing going during load shedding in Pakistan: what needs a UPS, why the internet drops, and how an offline POS helps.
items.title: Billing during load shedding:
items.description: Load shedding causes two different problems at the counter: the power goes, and the internet goes. They need different fixes. Here is what to put on a UPS and what your POS should do on its own.

p: When the power goes, anything without a backup switches off, including your PCs, printer and router. When the power comes back, or even while you are on a UPS, the internet often stays down because the router or the exchange has no power. A good setup handles both.

article.h: What to put on a UPS
p: No software can bill on a PC that is switched off. Put the main PC, each counter PC, the receipt printer and the network switch that connects them on a UPS. Size the UPS for the longest outage your area usually gets. Laptops as counters help, because they have their own battery.

article.h: What the POS should do without internet
p: Choose a POS that keeps the shop's data on your own main PC, so billing, printing and stock work over your shop network with no internet at all. Sales then sync to the cloud when the connection is back. If your POS needs the internet for every bill, the queue stops each time the router does.

article.h: If the main PC goes off too
p: Even with a UPS, a main PC can fail. In ZAP POS, counters keep billing on their own for a few hours, print receipts and kitchen tickets, share their sales with each other so stock stays right, and send everything to the main PC when it is back.

article.h: FBR and the cloud can wait
p: Bills that must go to FBR are queued with a note on the receipt and sent once the internet returns. Your owner's view of sales catches up the same way. Nothing is lost and nothing is sent twice.

faq.q: Does ZAP POS work during a power cut?
faq.a: Only if your PCs have power. ZAP POS doesn't need the internet, so with the PCs, printer and network switch on a UPS, billing carries on while the router is off.

faq.q: What should I put on a UPS for my counter?
faq.a: The main PC, the counter PCs, the receipt printer and the network switch. The router is optional for billing with ZAP POS.

faq.q: Will my FBR invoices be lost when the internet is down?
faq.a: No. They wait in a queue, the receipt says they will be sent, and they go to FBR by themselves when the internet returns.

items.seoDescription: What POS software is, what it does for a shop, what hardware you need, and how to start. A plain guide for shop and restaurant owners.
items.title: What is POS software?
items.titleHighlight: A plain guide for shop owners.
items.description: POS means point of sale: the place where a customer pays. POS software is the program on the counter PC that makes the bill, takes the money and updates your stock. Here is what it does and what you need to start.

faq.q: Do I need a barcode scanner?
faq.a: No, but it makes billing faster and cuts typing mistakes. Without one, you can search by name or tap a product tile.

faq.q: Can I use my old Excel product list?
faq.a: Usually yes. Ask whether the POS imports from Excel. ZAP POS can import a product list so you do not type it again.

faq.q: Is POS software only for big shops?
faq.a: No. A single kiryana shop or cafe can use one. It matters more as you add products, counters or branches.

items.ctaTitle: See a POS on your own products
items.ctaText: Book a free demo and we'll help you set up your first products.

p: A POS replaces the register and the notebook. The cashier scans or taps a product, the bill is added up, the customer pays, and the stock goes down by exactly what was sold. At the end of the day the sales, the cash and the stock all come from the same record, so they agree.
Better systems also record who sold what, who gave a discount, which bills were cancelled and which items were returned, so the owner can check without standing at the counter.

A Windows PC or laptop at the counter. A receipt printer and a [barcode](/barcode-system-for-your-shop) scanner make billing much faster but are not required: products can also be found by name or tapped on screen. A cash drawer is useful if you take a lot of cash. Put the PC on a UPS so a short power cut does not end the day.
Then you need your product list: names, prices and, if you have them, barcodes. If it is already in Excel, a good POS can import it so you do not type it again.

A POS does not count your stock for you if you never add what you buy. It only knows what you tell it: purchases in, sales out, returns back. Keep the purchase entries up to date and the stock numbers will be trustworthy.
It also does not remove the need for a good cashier. It makes mistakes easier to see and harder to hide.

It depends on the software. Many cloud systems stop when the internet goes. In Pakistan, where the connection drops often, ask whether billing carries on without it and syncs later. ZAP POS runs on your own PC and keeps billing when the internet drops. A power cut still turns the PC off, so a UPS matters.

Write down how your shop really sells: how many counters, whether you use barcodes, whether you need FBR invoicing, and how many branches. Then try a demo with your own products and a busy hour in mind. Our guide to choosing POS software in Pakistan lists the ten questions to ask.
Start with one counter and a short product list, bill on it for a week alongside your old method, then switch fully.

items.shortAnswer: POS software is the program at your counter that bills customers, records payments and updates stock in one step. You need a Windows PC, ideally a barcode scanner and a receipt printer, and software that keeps working when the internet drops.

items.title: Set up barcodes in your shop.
items.description: Barcodes make billing faster and stock more accurate. This guide shows how to put them on every product, including the ones that arrive without one.

faq.q: Can two products share one barcode?
faq.a: No. Each item, and each size or colour of it, should have its own barcode, or the stock cannot be right.

faq.q: Do I need to label every product before I start?
faq.a: No. Start with your fastest-selling items and keep the rest searchable by name. Add barcodes as you go.

faq.q: Which scanner should I buy?
faq.a: A standard USB barcode scanner works with most POS software. Check your POS's hardware list first; ZAP POS lists supported printers and scanners on its printers and scanners page.

items.ctaTitle: Try barcode billing with ZAP POS
items.ctaText: Book a free demo and we'll show you how to make and print your own labels.

article.h: Step 1: use the barcodes you already have
p: Most packaged goods already carry a barcode from the maker. Scan it once into your POS and enter the name and price. From then on, scanning the pack finds the product. This is the biggest saving: do these first.

article.h: Step 2: make your own for everything else
p: Loose items, items you repack, clothes, shoes and many accessories have no barcode. Give each a short code of your own and print it as a label. Keep one rule: one barcode for one item. If a shirt comes in three sizes and two colours, each size and colour gets its own barcode, so the stock for each is correct.
ZAP POS can make a barcode for an item, including each size and colour, and print its price tag on a label printer.

article.h: Step 3: get the right scanner and printer
p: A USB barcode scanner works like a keyboard and is the simplest choice. For labels you need a label printer; for bills, a thermal receipt printer. Check that your POS supports the models you plan to buy before you pay for them.

Stick labels where the scanner can read them: flat, not over folds or curves. Scan a few products at the counter and check the name and price come up right. Fix wrong prices now, not in front of a customer.

When a price changes, change it in the POS and reprint the tag. Remove old labels before sticking new ones. Never reuse a barcode for a different product. Print a few spare labels for items that sell fast.

items.shortAnswer: Use the manufacturer's barcode where a product has one. For loose or unlabelled products, make your own barcode, print it on a label, and stick it on. Scan every barcode once into your POS with its name and price, then bill by scanning.

items.seoDescription: Why shop stock never matches and how to fix it: record purchases and returns, count by section, watch low stock and expiry.
items.title: Stock that matches the shelf.
items.titleHighlight: How to count and control it.
items.description: Most shops lose money on stock they cannot see: units that were sold without a bill, bought without an entry, or went past their date. These habits fix most of it.

faq.q: How often should I count stock?
faq.a: A small section every day or week is better than the whole shop once a year. Fast sellers and expensive items deserve more frequent counts.

faq.q: Why does my stock differ from the system?
faq.a: Usually an unrecorded purchase or return, a product with two barcodes, a wrong size or colour, or items damaged or expired and not written off.

faq.q: Can ZAP POS stop me selling an out-of-stock product?
faq.a: Yes. A product that tracks stock cannot be sold once it reaches zero, and low-stock and expiry warnings help you reorder or return it in time.

items.ctaTitle: Get your stock under control
items.ctaText: Book a free demo and we'll show you stock, low-stock warnings and expiry alerts.

p: Stock goes wrong in three ways: something is sold without a bill, something is bought or returned without an entry, or something is damaged, expired or taken and nobody writes it down. A POS fixes the first by making every sale a bill. The other two need habits.
Enter every purchase as it arrives, by scanning what is on the delivery. Enter customer returns the same day. If stock is only added at month end, every count in between is wrong.

article.h: Count a little at a time
p: Counting the whole shop once a year is slow and everyone is tired. Instead count one shelf or section a day and compare it with what the system says. A small difference is easy to trace; a year of differences is not.

When the count and the system disagree, check the common causes first: a product with two [barcode](/barcode-system-for-your-shop)s, a size or colour sold under the wrong item, a return not entered, or a pack sold as single pieces. Then adjust the stock and write down why.

Know what is about to run out before a customer asks for it. For medicines, cosmetics and food, also watch dates: ZAP POS refuses to sell an expired product and lists items expiring within 30 days so you can return them to the supplier in time.
Limit who can cancel a bill, give a discount or return an item, and require a manager for the risky ones. When these are recorded with a name, mistakes and theft both become visible.

items.shortAnswer: Record every purchase and return, count one section of the shop at a time instead of everything at once, compare the count with the system, and investigate differences while they are small. Watch low stock and expiry dates.

features.title: Send
features.text: A manager picks the branch, scans or searches the products and presses Send. The stock leaves that branch at once and a slip prints. Sending works even when the internet is down; it is delivered at the next sync.

features.title: A number you can trace
features.text: Slips are numbered like LHR-2026-0007, per branch and per year. A cancelled number is kept, so there are no unexplained gaps.

features.title: Receive and count
features.text: The receiving branch sees the transfer as incoming, counts what really arrived and receives it into stock. Fewer units than sent is recorded as short and shown to the owner.

features.title: Cancel or send back
features.text: The sender can cancel a transfer that has not been received, and the receiver can send it all back. Either way the stock returns to the sender. Both need internet so the two branches cannot disagree.

features.text: The owner console at zappos.pk/account lists the transfers between the shop's branches: on the way, received, short, cancelled or sent back.

faq.q: Does it need internet?
faq.a: Sending does not: the stock leaves the sender and the transfer is delivered at the next sync. Receiving, cancelling and sending back need internet, so that two branches acting at the same moment cannot both be right.

faq.q: Which products can be transferred?

faq.q: Can I send stock to a branch of another owner?
faq.a: No. Transfers only work between branches of the same owner account.

faq.q: What if fewer units arrive than were sent?
faq.a: The receiver enters the count. The difference is recorded as short on the transfer and shown to the owner. Nothing is changed or deleted afterwards.

faq.q: Do older versions still work?
faq.a: Yes. A branch on an older version keeps billing normally; it just cannot send or receive transfers until its main PC is updated to 1.9.149 or newer.

p: We count visits anonymously: a random browser id kept in your browser, the kind of device, the website that sent you and any campaign tag in the link. We don't record your name, your IP address or the full pages you visit in these counts.
When you book a demo, we keep what you type in the form (name, mobile number, email, shop, city and message) so we can contact you. Visitors can't read other people's requests.
If you create an account, we keep your email address and a protected password to sign you in, and the details of your plan and payments so you can see them in your account.

Your shop's data (products, bills, stock, customers and staff) is kept on your own main PC. When the internet is available, a copy of the records needed for your account and licence is sent to ZAP POS's cloud. During setup, the owner's name, mobile number, email and shop name are sent to us so we can issue and support your licence.
If you switch on FBR or PRA reporting, your bills are sent to the tax authority as the law requires.
The website runs on Vercel and our database and sign-in run on Supabase. We don't sell your information or share it for advertising.
You can ask us what we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it where we are not required to keep it. Contact us on WhatsApp or by email, and we'll reply.

items.title: The rules,
items.description: What you can expect from ZAP POS and what we ask of you, in plain words.

p: A ZAP POS plan gives your shop the right to use the software on the counters your plan allows. A shop has one active plan at a time, and the plan sets how many counters you can pair with your main PC.
The licence is for your own shop or chain. Please don't share your licence key or resell the software.
Your products, bills, customers and staff belong to you and are kept on your own main PC. We use the copy in our cloud only to show you your account and branches, and to support you when you ask.
Bills, invoices, payments and stock records are never deleted by the app. They are cancelled or reversed, so your history stays complete.
Payments for your plan are recorded by us when you pay; the website does not take online payments. Each paid period has a start and an end date, and periods for one shop don't overlap.
To switch plans, we end the current period first and then start the new one.
The price of a plan is shown before you buy, and that price is final. Once a licence is purchased, it can't be refunded, so please try the demo and ask us your questions before you pay.

Keep your main PC backed up and your staff PINs private. Check your tax settings, such as FBR or PRA reporting, with your accountant. You are responsible for the prices, taxes and bills you issue to your own customers.
We help with setup and problems through WhatsApp and email. We may improve the software and these terms over time, and the date at the top of this page shows the latest version.

We work hard to keep ZAP POS reliable, but no software is perfect. ZAP POS is provided as it is, and we are not responsible for losses caused by things outside our control, such as hardware failure, power cuts or internet outages. Offline billing keeps your counters selling when the internet drops, but it can't run on a PC that has no power.
These terms are governed by the laws of Pakistan.

items.shortAnswer: ZAP POS is point of sale software for shops in Pakistan, made in Lahore. It runs on Windows PCs, keeps billing without internet, sends bills to FBR or PRA, and lets several counters share one live stock.

specs.label: Tax
specs.value: FBR and PRA invoicing built in

p: ZAP POS is point of sale software that a shop installs on its own Windows PCs. One PC in each branch is the main PC and holds the shop's data; the other PCs are counters that bill through it over the shop's network.

Kiryana and general stores, supermarkets, pharmacies and medical stores, bakeries and sweet shops, clothing and shoe shops (stock by size and colour), and restaurants and cafes, from a single counter to [several counters](/multi-counter-pos) and branches.

Billing by [barcode](/barcode-system-for-your-shop), search or product tiles, with holds, discounts, returns and quick sales. Stock with packs (dozen, carton, strip, box), items sold by weight, expiry dates that block sales, low-stock levels, purchases and supplier ledgers. Restaurant tables, takeaway, delivery and kitchen printers by station. Sales tax by payment method and sending bills to FBR with the invoice number and QR code on the receipt. Staff PIN logins, manager approvals, cash per shift, daily reports, barcode labels, nightly backups and automatic updates.

The internet is never needed to make a bill. If the main PC goes off, counters keep billing on their own for a few hours and send their bills back when it returns, each saved exactly once. FBR bills made offline are queued and sent later.

Versions for Mac or Android counters and an Urdu interface (the app is in English) are planned. A dedicated owner app is coming soon for Android, with an iPhone app planned after that. Until then the owner signs in at zappos.pk/account on any phone or computer and sees every branch.

Plans are Dukaan (one shop, one counter), Brand (several counters, priced per branch) and Enterprise (4 or more branches, custom price), billed monthly or yearly in rupees. Setup needs a licence key from ZAP POS, and help is given over WhatsApp.

faq.q: What is ZAP POS?
faq.a: Point of sale software for shops in Pakistan, made in Lahore. It runs on Windows PCs and keeps billing without internet.

faq.q: Does ZAP POS work offline?
faq.a: Yes. Billing never needs the internet, and counters keep billing for a few hours even if the main PC goes off.

faq.q: Is ZAP POS FBR integrated?
faq.a: Yes. It can send each bill to FBR and print FBR's invoice number and QR code on the receipt.

faq.q: Does ZAP POS handle sizes and colours?
faq.a: Yes. A product can have up to two options (Size and Colour by default, renamable), and each combination has its own barcode, price and stock. Made for clothing and shoe shops.

faq.q: Which businesses use ZAP POS?
faq.a: Kiryana stores, supermarkets, pharmacies, bakeries, clothing and shoe shops, restaurants and cafes, from one counter to several branches.

faq.q: Can ZAP POS move stock between branches?
faq.a: Yes. From version 1.9.149 a manager can send stock to another branch of the same owner. It leaves the sender at once, a numbered slip prints, and the receiving branch counts what arrived. A short count is recorded, never hidden.

faq.q: Can the owner see all branches from a phone?
faq.a: Yes. The owner signs in at zappos.pk/account with the same login as ZAP POS and sees today's sales of every branch, each branch on its own, top sellers, low stock, stock transfers and the plan.

items.description: Dukaandaar jo sawal humein WhatsApp par poochte hain, unke seedhe jawab Roman Urdu mein.
items.shortAnswer: ZAP POS Pakistan ki dukaanon ke liye POS software hai. Bill banane ke liye internet nahi chahiye, FBR ko bill bhej sakta hai, aur kai counters ek hi stock par chalte hain.

faq.q: POS software kya hota hai?
faq.a: POS (point of sale) software dukaan ke counter par bill banata hai, bechi hui cheezein stock se kam karta hai aur din ki sale ka hisaab rakhta hai. Register aur calculator ki jagah ek screen.

faq.q: Kya ZAP POS internet ke baghair chalta hai?
faq.a: Ji haan. Bill banane ke liye internet ki zaroorat nahi. Bill, receipt, stock aur reports dukaan ke network par chalte hain, aur internet wapas aane par cloud mein chale jate hain.

faq.q: Load shedding mein billing kaise chalegi?
faq.a: Bijli jaane par PC band ho jata hai, is liye main PC, counters, printer aur network switch UPS par lagayein. ZAP POS ko internet nahi chahiye, to router band hone par bhi billing chalti rehti hai.

faq.q: Kya ZAP POS FBR ke saath kaam karta hai?
faq.a: Ji haan. ZAP POS har bill FBR ko bhej sakta hai aur receipt par FBR ka invoice number aur QR code print karta hai. Internet na ho to bill baad mein khud chala jata hai.

faq.q: Ek dukaan mein kitne counters chala sakte hain?
faq.a: Jitne aapka plan allow kare. Sab counters ek hi stock aur prices istemal karte hain, aur sale chand second mein har counter par nazar aati hai.

faq.q: Main PC band ho jaye to kya hoga?
faq.a: Counters kuch ghante khud billing karte rehte hain aur main PC wapas aane par sab bills bhej dete hain. Koi bill do dafa save nahi hota.

faq.q: Kaun se printer aur scanner chalte hain?
faq.a: Aam thermal receipt printer (80 ya 58 mm, USB ya network), USB barcode scanner, cash drawer aur label printer.

faq.q: Kya expired dawai bik sakti hai?
faq.a: Nahi. Product par expiry date daalein; date guzarne ke baad ZAP POS usay bill mein add nahi karne deta.

faq.q: ZAP POS kahan se milega?
faq.a: Website ke Download page se. Setup ke liye licence key chahiye; key na ho to setup mein WhatsApp button dabayein, hum bhej denge.

faq.q: Kya ek branch se doosri branch ko stock bheja ja sakta hai?
faq.a: Ji haan. ZAP POS 1.9.149 se manager apni doosri branch ko stock bhej sakta hai. Stock usi waqt bhejne wali branch se kam ho jata hai, number wali parchi print hoti hai, aur dosri branch gin kar receive karti hai. Kam aaya to wo likha jata hai, chhupaya nahi jata.

faq.q: Kya owner sab branches phone par dekh sakta hai?
faq.a: Ji haan. Owner zappos.pk/account par ZAP POS wale login se sign in kare to har branch ki aaj ki sale, top bikne wali cheezein, kam stock aur stock transfers dekh sakta hai.
